long_biography.plain_text:
When Elekta nearly ran out of working capital in 1979, Laurent Leksell took a personal bank loan and bought his siblings' shares. The move preserved a small business built around his father's surgical inventions. Progress remained slow until Leksell left a successful consulting career after his father's death in 1986 and committed himself to Elekta full time.

He led Elekta as chief executive, using a stock-market listing and acquisitions to extend its work from Gamma Knife radiosurgery into broader radiation oncology. Leksell now chairs the company and has also founded Leksell Social Ventures, which applies patient capital and outcomes-based financing to life-science and Swedish social-welfare projects.
